title: Oil Prices Are Climbing, Yet These 3 Energy Stocks Yield 3%+
author: Na
description: Oil prices have climbed to three-month highs due to Middle East tensions and disrupted Gulf crude flows. For investors seeking energy exposure without relying solely on oil price appreciation, dividend-paying energy stocks like Kinder Morgan, Chevron, and Canadian Natural Resources offer recurring income and diversified cash flows with yields above 3%.

title: 1 No-Brainer ETF I'm Loading Up on in 2026 and Beyond
author: Stefon Walters
description: The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) is recommended as a core holding for long-term investors seeking diversified dividend income. With a 3% dividend yield (three times higher than S&P 500 ETFs), low 0.06% expense ratio, and exposure to stable sectors like healthcare and consumer staples, SCHD offers attractive passive income potential. The ETF has delivered 29% total returns year-to-date and is particularly suitable for tax-advantaged accounts like Roth IRAs.

title: Chevron's Venezuela JV Expansion: Time to Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
author: Zacks.Com
description: Chevron plans over $7 billion in Venezuela investment targeting 600,000 barrels per day production, leveraging strong Q2 cash flow and faster-than-expected Hess synergies. However, the stock trades at a premium valuation compared to peers Eni and Repsol while facing geopolitical and execution risks in Venezuela. Analysts recommend a Hold rating, suggesting existing shareholders stay invested but new investors wait for better valuations.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong fundamentals including $22.6B operating cash flow, record production growth, and successful Hess synergies are offset by premium valuation (P/E 13.68), underperformance versus peers, and significant Venezuela geopolitical/execution risks. Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) reflects balanced risk-reward.

Significant Venezuelan exposure with 50% stake in Cardón IV and exclusive operator of Junín-5 area (35 billion barrels). Stock outperformed CVX with 54.6% gain over past year and trades at lower forward P/E of 10.08, suggesting better valuation.

title: 2 Safe High-Yield Energy Dividend Stocks You've Probably Never Heard Of
author: Leo Sun
description: The article highlights two overlooked energy dividend stocks: Kimbell Royalty Partners, which owns mineral rights to 17 million acres and generates steady cash from oil and gas production with a 10.75% dividend yield, and Williams Companies, a midstream pipeline operator with exposure to the AI boom through data center natural gas supply, offering a 2.76% yield with strong growth prospects.

title: Chevron Stayed in Venezuela for 20 Years While Rivals Left. Here's Why Its CEO Says Patience Pays Off.
author: Matt Dilallo
description: Chevron has signed a landmark deal to significantly expand its Venezuela operations and double output over five years, capitalizing on its decision to remain in the country after rivals ExxonMobil and ConocoPhillips exited in 2007. The company plans to invest over $7 billion to increase production to 600,000 barrels per day with costs under $20 per barrel, positioning it ahead of competitors now evaluating re-entry.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Chevron's patience in Venezuela is paying off with a landmark expansion deal, improved fiscal terms, planned $7B investment, and significant production growth potential (280K to 600K barrels/day) at low costs, providing competitive advantage over rivals.

ConocoPhillips exited Venezuela in 2007 and has been pursuing a $12B arbitration award. Like ExxonMobil, it is evaluating potential re-entry but remains significantly behind Chevron's established position.
